notes:
40 stations, nos. 81-120, under "West Coast of Scotland" with three sub-headings: "Mainland" (81-82), "Outer Hebrides" (83-88) and "Mainland, Skye, and Inner Hebrides" (89-120). No light characters are printed. The "other" column is the height column; after the first row it mostly uses a ditto mark (") for "ft.". I copied that as printed.

MARKS / YEARS: The asterisk columns sit under the header "1879, '80, '81, '82." The 'marks' field keeps the asterisks with their printed spacing; the fragments keep the full line, including leading spaces. Each asterisk's position gives its year:
- All four years: 83, 86, 93(+94 by brace), 95, 96, 102, 103, 112, 113, 114.
- 1879/'80/'81: 81, 82, 85, 100, 111.
- '80/'81/'82: 90 (the third asterisk is one space right of the '82 column but clearly belongs to '82), 98, 101.
- '80/'81: 84, 87, 91, 110.
- 1879/'80: 92, 99, 104.
- '81 only: 109, 115.
- None: 88, 89, 97, 105-108, 116-120.

KEEPER NAMES: Most keeper names end in a full stop ("J. Youngclause.", "D. McCulloch." etc.). "Alex. Thompson" doesn't. I treated the final stop as row punctuation and left it out of 'keepers'. The fragments keep it. "John Ewing" is printed for both Dhuheartach (95) and Skervuile (102). It could be one man or two; I didn't merge them.

BRACES:
- Monach Island (86): two heights are braced together ({ 150 " } / { 62 " }), probably the two lights. The second height line has no station of its own, so I kept it as a second fragment of row 86.
- Hynish Signal Tower (93) and Skerryvore (94): a brace joins them. The asterisks, "150 \"" and "Alx. McEachern." are printed only on 93's line. I gave the keeper only to 93, as printed, but the brace suggests they belong to both. Hynish was the Skerryvore shore station.
- Nos. 116-120: braced to one "Isle of Man." printed on 118's line, so I gave place "Isle of Man" to all five. The coast field still shows the Scottish sub-heading they sit under. The text after the list says these five "are now placed at the head of the W. of England stations under Mr. P. Kermode."

COPIED AS PRINTED, POSSIBLY ERRORS:
- "Rona, Sye": probably Skye. I put "Sye" in place.
- "Island Glass": elsewhere Glas/Ghlais.
- "Ardnamurchan, Pt. Argyle": the comma looks misplaced (Ardnamurchan Pt., Argyle). I split at the printed comma (name "Ardnamurchan", place "Pt. Argyle").
- "Rosshire", "Tyree", "Argyle", "Lochindaul", "Chickens Rock", "Mac Arthur's Head": spelled as printed.
- "Longness L.V.": Langness is a lighthouse, so the L.V. type and the spelling may both be slips.
- "119.-1880. Bahama Rock L.V.": I took the number as "119" and put "-1880." in other. It may mean the vessel was listed or changed in 1880, but I'm not sure.

I didn't split out "Dhuheartach, S. of Ross of Mull" either: it wraps onto two lines, and the place is "S. of Ross of Mull", joined from both lines.
